I disagree with you on point number 4. I've seen too many avis where the "Quest Optimization" is changing out shaders. No decimation, no reduction in toggles. Just port it straight across. 

Specifically the last Quest avatar I asked about had 158,886 polygons, 21 skinned meshes and 60 material slots. Unsurprisingly these were the same numbers I got when I checked avatar stats on my PC!

The polygon limit for Poor on Quest is 20,000. See: https://creators.vrchat.com/avatars/avatar-performance-ranking-system/

@{62df7cd83e007e467295c4e1|full_name}: u still need to Activate the avi to see poor avatars the point is 20k is to low

The best u can get to still see an avatar without activ

ating It is 15k polygons soo uk

90% of the Quest avis r Very poor

You can't compare a processor that is dedicated mostly to render 2D and 3D graphics to a mobile processor, that are very limited and do not have 3D graphics as a high priority. 

You are saying that a device with a single processor and only a few watts should have to process the same as a device with hundreds of watts available and different dedicated processors. 

Also, that a game is not competitive does not mean it can have a low framerate, just because i don't need fast reaction times from my device it doesn't mean it's ok if my battery is about to explode and my processor is about to desolder from the pcb.

Very poor doesn't equal quality content, there's no relation between quality and stats, unless it's performance wise, which in this case very poor means bad quality.

If a creator put tons of hours on optimizing avatars for quest it wouldn't be very poor on the first place. Just because on pc you can have avatars with a lot of things it doesn't mean that it should be the same on mobile. It might take time to optimize an avatar, but it's possible, not hard (just slow), what happens is that people want the avatar to be as customizable as a character editor on some AAA game, on a mobile device.

20k polygons is enough, if not more than i expected for mobile
